hints: Focus on what you feel, the pad gets hotter, so think about which way heat energy is flowing.
Iron in air with water and oxygen turns to rusted iron oxide, so work out the oxidation number change for iron.
Link heat release to exo or endo, and link increase in oxidation number to loss or gain of electrons to complete the description.
walkthrough:
**Decide if heat is released or absorbed**

The pad gets hotter when exposed to air. That means chemical energy is being converted to heat energy and given out to the surroundings.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{exothermic = gives out heat, temperature rises}$$

**Identify what happens to iron**

Iron reacts with oxygen from the air in the presence of water. This is rusting, forming hydrated iron(III) oxide.

Simplified overall change:
$$4\text{Fe} + 3\text{O}_{2} + x\text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}_{2}\text{O}_{3}\cdot x\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$$

**Track the electrons**

In this change iron goes from $\text{Fe}$ with oxidation number 0 to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ in the oxide with oxidation number +3. An increase in oxidation number is oxidation, which is loss of electrons.

Half-equation idea:
$$\text{Fe} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + 3e^{-}$$

**Put the two ideas together**

Heat is given out, so exothermic. Iron is oxidised, so it loses electrons. That combination matches the correct description.

options.A: Incorrect. Endothermic means heat is taken in and the surroundings get colder, but the pad gets hotter. Iron gaining electrons would be reduction, but iron is oxidised to rust here.
options.B: Incorrect. It is right that iron loses electrons by oxidation, but endothermic is wrong. A reaction that makes the pad hotter must be giving out heat, so it is exothermic.
options.C: Incorrect. It is right that the reaction is exothermic because heat is released, but iron gaining electrons is reduction. Here $\text{Fe}(0)$ changes to $\text{Fe}(+3)$, which is loss of electrons.
options.D: Correct. The pad getting hotter shows heat energy is released, so exothermic. Iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide, oxidation number rises from 0 to +3, so iron is oxidised and loses electrons.
